newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 20.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Thursday's Daily Variety:

* NEW YORK - Court TV founder and chairman Steven Brill is quitting the cable network and its sibling publisher, American Lawyer Media, after unsuccessfully attempting a buyout of the two businesses from Time Warner. Time Warner Vice Chairman Ted Turner is understood to have vetoed Brill's attempt at a buyout, apparently anxious to retain some control of the cable network, which at times has drawn viewers away from CNN. Time Warner owns one-third of Court TV and a majority of American Lawyer.

* NEW YORK - NBC's "Asteroid" garnered the highest rating for any network multiple-parter since May 1994's "The Stand" from ABC, NBC's best multiple-part 18-49 rating since May 1988's "Something Is Out There" and the network's strongest February multi rating since '84's "Celebrity."

* HOLLYWOOD - Silver King Broadcasting SKTV.O has made three key hires, including veteran print journalist and TV news producer Bill Knoedelseder as Vice President of news, where he will oversee the creation of news operations for the group owner's 12 major-market TV stations.

* HOLLYWOOD - Samuel L. Jackson and Greta Scacchi are set to play "The Red Violin" for New Line International and three other overseas companies in New Line's first international co-production, the company announced Wednesday.
* NEW YORK - Warner Bros. purchased the new Nicholas Sparks romance novel, Message in a Bottle, for $1.5 million, sources said.
* HOLLYWOOD - Michael Ovitz, a graduate of the University o California at Los Angeles, has committed to a $25 million gift to UCLA's Medical Center.
